Causes: Fungal pathogen overwinters in fallen leaves and fruit; Spreads by wind and rain to new growth.
Description: Olive-green to brown velvety spots on leaves; yellowing and premature leaf drop; fruit develops corky spots.
Cures/Management: Remove infected leaves/fruit; prune for airflow; avoid overhead watering (don't allow leaves to stay wet); apply fungicides in spring.
Notes: Fungicides are not recommended for non-ornamental trees.

Causes: Rust fungus requiring plants from two different families (Cupressaceae and Rosaceae); spreads via wind from galls; Trees and shrubs often tolerate infection
Description: Yellow-orange spots on leaves, later red raised lesions; fruit may develop spots; heavy infection causes defoliation.
Cures/Management: Remove galls on nearby Juniper and red cedar trees; Remove infected twigs/branches on Rosaceae plants; apply fungicides at bud break.
Notes: Fungicides are not recommended for non-ornamental trees.
